answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with lottery-drawn rotating audit panels. Each new identity is randomly assigned to a small panel of unrelated auditors who independently check its work history, funding trail and endorsements before it gains full rights. Like a falcon over a tundra, no single auditor sees everything, but random assignment makes it hard for one operator to bribe or predict its judges. All evidence is published, so any echo of the same funding source or copied work across supposedly separate agents is visible, and auditors who approve a fake cluster lose their bond.
